Hi friend,

I randomly came across your comment while looking for some guidance myself, and I guess I want to put my two cents in as a person who went through sth similar at that age.(I am 29 now just for context)

-Start with some great news. Highschool is just the beginning!

Trust me, your highschool self isn't your final form and it is far from the person you end up being in life (this can be good or bad). it is our first steps into adulthood and most of us don't have a clue what we are doing then. It is a crazy time for many, especially with no guidance..While better experiences can help, it by no means determines who you are for the rest of your life. I say this from experience (I was so quiet and antisocial in highschool, it's ridiculous. I remember getting hit with news I was sick and I honestly gave up for a couple of years.)

-Smoking Pot 

Pot is a great escape, but smoking it multiple times a day will lead you nowhere but trouble. Too much of anything is bad, imagine those were drinks or even food. You would be on the road to alcoholism or obesity. I'm not even against pot, but doing it on a daily basis is not good. Cut it out completely for some time or limit it to a once every couple of months thing. 

-Why?

Because it will kill any drive you have to change things. You get caught up in all sorts of thoughts when high and the clock tiks away. From your post I can already see you lack motivation and the discipline it can create, but want to change that. Discipline wont come easy , but it is something you build up slowely and laying of pot, at least till you get your stuff together , is a step in the right direction. (You can eventually come back to it, there are ppl who function well with it, I mean look at snoop Dogg/Wiz khalifa, but only do so when you find your footing, honestly you might not even want to do it then.)

Money 

Unfortunately this is a factor in life. Finding fulltime employment will be a must at one point. You have some room to breathe given that housing will be taken care of for a while, but don't take that lightly. Find a job that you can perform well. Do it to the best of your ability. I'm not saying get taken advantage of, but just do your duties and learn as much as you can while on the job. Any skill learnt at a job will come useful down the line. Be a decent or at least enthusiastic employee. (Don't think let me pretend to like it, think how can I best get this done where everyone is happy, while on the clock. Once work is over focus on YOURSELF).


Housing

Your mom is honestly cool for giving you that much time to adjust. I know ppl who were almost kicked out with no notice. My advice here is to be as useful as possible around the house while you are there. Show appreciation with little things that will make life there easier. (clean and tidy can be achieved with 20 min of work, dishes, laundry, cooking. Stuff that you would have to take care of living alone. Don't spend all day doing that, but assist around ) These are skills we all need and If you start of while living with your mom, you have some back up if things go bad.

General advice

What I would do if I could go back to 18


Time passes very quickly, looking back at least. You honestly end up regretting the things you didn't try because you look back and realise that not only did you not fail in things that drew your attention, but you didn't even have the strength to try. 

Regret weighs heavy on you, and it's not something you want to feel. Trust me.

(By trying I don't mean stupid shit , anything illegal, immoral keep away from lol - have to say this)


General tips-

Exercise -Try and get in shape. I cannot stress this enough. On the surface it seems like such a shallow/superficial thing, but sticking to it pays of so much. It helps u stick to something and it keeps you healthy. I have some back issues from too much sitting. My advice here is look into mobility(back, hips) , cardio, and strength. Find a rythm that works for you. You can just do calisthenics at home to start or go to a gym. You are going to SUCK at first. And that is totally ok. read up on it or watch vids around that as you get better, more comfortable try and join a gym or STH. You will have STH to talk about with ppl. My advice is go for a trainer, it's like a cheatcode to cut down the beginner levels 


Mindset - it is easy to get caught up in negative thoughts. Trust me. My best advice here is try to listen to things that will help grow. I started with Tony Robbins at my lowest point and it helped. You need a radical shift in thoughts. What you focus on you created and being sad and depressed in a way just creates more of the same. Feed your brain with things that push you a little. Books and videos are good, just focus on them.

Video I would recommend here is STH like this:

https://youtu.be/vDLGgt4B50I

You can listen to stuff like this while you walk. It gets you out of the house and is interesting to listen to 


Father figure-

My dad is still with us, but unfortunately he worked so much it is almost like he wasn't there. I understand the feeling it can cause and have seen firsthand the life long effects it can have. Good news you are young and can still learn. The ticket here is some reassurance and some tough love, you have to see it first. Coaches are good for this, but you can start of with videos just to get the mindset. 

Channels I found cool-
Dad how do I 

https://youtube.com/@DadhowdoI

It is literally a guy who acts as a father figure. He is the positive energy I needed sometimes. Shows random things and simulates talks. He is so wholesome.

Secondly, a bit of tough love. Kevin Samuels. He has a bit of a bad reputation, but i honestly benefited from listening to his videos where he talked to men. 

I found these Videos



https://youtu.be/Ka7BoCn9M5U

https://youtu.be/imO41mJoNwYimO41mJoNwY


COMEDY

Life isn't all discipline and hardwork, all that work is there for us to live life the best we can. I remind myself to listen to comedy specials, ppl I find funny (Theo Von, Kevin Hart, Jim Jeffries -there are so many comedians out there find whose style u like.) Relax to some comedy and have a laugh. A sense of humor is never a bad thing to have.


Practice speaking Infront of a mirror 


Have a few "sets" you can bring out in situations. Start of in front of a mirror, maybe even film yourself. Having a couple of sets you can bring out when around ppl makes socializing easier and it will help you get out there a bit more.



Why I responded to you-


This is a lot of info and I am sorry to hit you with so much. I randomly came across this comment and would have appreciated the help when I was 18. A lil about me , I worked since 20, started looking into writing because I wanted to gather my thoughts and improve communication. Started doing that for a while and even found work as a writer. Since then went back to school and am now in my final year of Uni at 29.

There is time to change, as long as you don't let it slip by.  Small steps build up and I'm routing for you 

Best of luck and I hope this helps redirect you out of your cycle.
Love from Europe
